references.text: Then the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and while he slept, He took one of his ribs and closed up its place with flesh. This verse is the direct precursor to 2:22 and describes how God took the rib that He formed into a woman.

Then the man said, 'This time it is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.' Adam's response as God brings the woman to him, a direct follow-up to 2:22.
God created mankind in His own image, in the image of God He created them; male and female He created them. A summary of the creation of man and woman in chapter 1, which is detailed further in 2:22.
For man did not come from woman, but woman from man; neither was man created for woman, but woman for man. Paul refers directly to Gen 2:22 regarding that woman was created from man.

Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh. This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church. Paul quotes Gen 2:24 and places the creation of man and woman in a christological context.
For Adam was formed first, then Eve. Paul refers to the order of creation as described in Gen 2:21-22.
He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the Lord. Reflects the theme that God brought the woman to man as a gift.
5:2 confirms that the formation of the woman in 2:22 was part of God's original blessing and plan for humanity.
Mark 10:6 uses the formation of the woman from the man as a theological basis for the indissolubility of marriage.
1 Cor 11:12 interprets and applies the order of creation from 2:22 in a theological discussion about the mutuality of the sexes.
